label: L=9 copy step 2 (re-reading orig token 0 while outputting token 1), gated by token content
explanation: Very sparse (about 0.4% of eligible steps). Fires only at the copy step with recall_idx == 1, i.e. the step right after the first copied output, where the input is orig(0) and the output is orig(1). 95% of activations and 96% of mass are at L=9 (t=10). The rest are at L=8, and there are none for L<=7, in the original phase, or at the delimiter. Within that slot it fires on only about 2.3% of sequences. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on the content of the first few original tokens. It is enriched when the input/first token is v, r, g, j or o (top examples are mostly j/v/g) and when orig(1)/orig(2) are f, h, n, 0 or 1 (the top examples look like v h f ..., j h f ..., g h 1 f ...). This looks like a graded sum over token identities rather than a crisp rule. Location alone gives recall 0.95 with precision 0.02. Adding the token sets gives F1 about 0.34 (precision 0.25, recall 0.54, mass recall 0.61). Requiring all three token conditions raises precision to 0.57 but drops recall to 0.12.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=v (+3.33), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=r (+2.92), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=j (+2.34), next_out=1 (+2.27), orig3=q (+1.97), next_out=f (+1.96). Lower it: orig7=- (-2.98), orig1=v (-1.95), orig3=z (-1.87), orig3=i (-1.76).
